tips.title: Resume Tips
tips.subtitle: Guidance to make each section shine

general.title: General
items: Keep your resume to 1-2 pages and lead with your strongest content.
Use consistent formatting, tense, and date styles throughout.
Tailor keywords to the job description to pass ATS screening.
Quantify achievements with numbers, percentages, and outcomes.

summary.title: Profile Summary
items: Open with your role, years of experience, and core specialty.
Highlight 2-3 signature achievements or strengths.
Keep it to 2-4 concise sentences focused on value.
Avoid generic buzzwords; be specific and results-driven.

experience.title: Work Experience
items: Start each bullet with a strong action verb (Led, Built, Reduced).
Show impact with metrics: revenue, time saved, users, growth.
Focus on achievements, not just responsibilities.
List roles in reverse-chronological order.

education.title: Education
items: List your highest or most relevant qualification first.
Include degree, institution, and graduation year.
Add honors, GPA, or relevant coursework when impressive.
Keep it concise once you have professional experience.

skills.title: Skills
items: Prioritize skills mentioned in the job description.
Group related skills and lead with your strongest.
Mix technical (hard) and interpersonal (soft) skills.
Avoid listing outdated or irrelevant tools.

projects.title: Projects
items: Describe the problem, your role, and the outcome.
Mention the tech stack and tools you used.
Link to live demos or repositories when possible.
Highlight measurable results or recognition.

languages.title: Languages
items: Use clear proficiency levels (Native, Professional, Conversational).
List languages relevant to the role or region.
Be honest about your proficiency.
Place near the bottom unless central to the job.

certifications.title: Certifications
items: Include the certification name and issuing body.
Prioritize current, industry-recognized credentials.
Add the year if recent or relevant.
Remove expired or low-value certifications.
